Also checked: Masterchow (pre-fund, D2C Asian food: different category), Acai Theory (health QSR, not packaged), DressFolk/Salty/Trisu/Everyday/NewMe/Krvvy/CUNIN/Ionic/&Done (non-food brands), Plazza/Cherry/Vaaree (commerce). Real revenue (INR 16.5 L in October, 3.4x since June) at 48% gross margin with positive contribution (R3, R5).
Candid about their risks and willing to share the cohort sheet and co-packer agreement (R1).
Squarely in a focus sector, with a team whose experience matches category and supply chain (S1, S3).
case_against: Growth is mostly bought: about 70% of new customers come from paid social or promoted quick commerce. The first order loses money and LTV:CAC is about 1.8x (R3).
Crowded, consolidating category (Tata Soulfull, ITC Yoga Bar, Slurrp Farm) with no articulated moat; three hero SKUs from one co-packer (R6, S4).
Capital intensity: 40% of the raise goes to inventory, and the scaled peer is still heavily loss-making, so this cheque risks being diluted (R5).
Possible overlap with portfolio brands Taakat and MomsMade needs a conversation first (G1).
call_questions: What is 90-day repeat for paid-social-acquired customers vs nutritionist-referred, and for Jowar puffs vs Ragi choco crunch?
Is the August cohort's 38% a full 90 days for every customer, and why does the deck show only that cohort?

Tata and ITC now own millet and better-for-you brands with national distribution. Why won't you be out-shelved within two years? (Pressure test on the weakest point.)

dossier.research_notes: Key finding: MeetRecord (now Outdoo AI), an All In Capital portfolio company per its June 2024 round coverage, does call transcription, summaries and CRM updates; the application does not mention it and claims no India-first competitor exists. Deck vs form: MRR 2.1 L vs 1.9 L (and 1.7 L from seats x price). Sector ticked as consumer tech; actually B2B SaaS. No founder/company footprint found. Web quotes were extracted via a fetch tool and should be re-verified with verify_web.

criteria.rationale: For an early B2B SaaS the defining risk is whether paid revenue is real and retained against well-funded competitors. The founders name operational risks (recording rules, noisy-call accuracy, BFSI concentration) but give no plan for any of them, report three different MRR figures across deck, form and their own seats x price, and state there is no India-first player when several exist, including the fund's own portfolio company. The revenue contradiction is a candour signal and pulls this down.

gates.detail: Conflict with portfolio company MeetRecord (now Outdoo AI), in which All In Capital invested and followed on in June 2024. MeetRecord transcribes sales calls, produces AI summaries and coaching and updates the CRM from the call: the same job for the same buyer (sales teams), even though MeetRecord focuses on US SMEs and Talkbook on Indian inside sales. The application does not mention MeetRecord. This is the C003 situation exactly. Rest of the portfolio checked: SalesMonk (AI pipeline generation) is next to it in the sales stack, not the same job. Mailmodo, BiteSpeed, RevenueHero and Rocketlane are other sales/marketing SaaS but none records or transcribes calls. Nothing else overlaps.

Does not depend on a permission that is withdrawn or not yet granted. Call-recording consent (DPDP duties from May 2027; telecom rules) is a compliance design task the founders already name as a risk, not a regulatory change the business needs.

The founders ticked 'Consumer tech', which is wrong: this is B2B SaaS. But the business really is Indian-language AI software, which the fund says it backs (~30% Indian AI) and has backed in sales SaaS, so the fit is real rather than a matter of the label. Recorded under S1.
Pre-seed, INR 2 Cr at INR 12 Cr post, with one other pre-seed fund in conversation. This is within the first-round size (up to ~INR 6 Cr) the fund leads.

case_for: Real early revenue: 16 paying teams and 340 seats in four months, mostly from founder outbound and referrals rather than paid acquisition (R2, R3).
Capital-efficient SaaS shape: founder-stated 70% gross margin and ~5-month payback mean INR 2 Cr can plausibly reach 80 teams (R5, S2).
On paper the team pairs a CRM product lead with a speech-ML engineer, the right two skills for code-mixed Indian sales calls (S3).
case_against: Portfolio conflict: MeetRecord/Outdoo, a fund portfolio company, does the same job for sales teams; the application does not mention it (G1).
Three different MRR figures (deck INR 2.1 L, form INR 1.9 L, seats x price INR 1.7 L) on the deciding metric: a candour question before anything else (R1, R3).
Founders say no India-first competitor exists while Convin, ConvoZen, Enthu.ai and MeetRecord are all live, and the only claimed moat (code-mixed accuracy) has no benchmark (R6, S4).
Founder backgrounds are unverifiable: employers not named, LinkedIn links are placeholders, no public footprint (S3).

gates.detail: Triggered as a precaution (the fund prefers a false alarm). Rocketpay (UdharPay), a portfolio company, helps businesses collect money owed to them via NACH mandates, so the customer is the same (Indian SMEs collecting receivables) and the job is close (getting paid on what customers owe). Settlr's payment links and collections do that job by a different rail. Mannjal (lending-out-of-the-box for B2B marketplaces) is adjacent on B2B working-capital credit. Kushal should confirm with both founders before any call. Rest of the portfolio checked: Volt, MoMoney, Returns, Prosparity and FuturElectra are consumer or EV finance. EximFiles, GloRoots and the B2B marketplaces (Magma, Hectar, FanTail, Nirmaan, Suite42) are not payments or receivables tools. No other overlap.

Works under existing rules through NBFC partners and a licensed payment aggregator. No favourable rule change is needed, though DLG caps and pool-account rules constrain the structure (scored under R1/R4).
Genuinely fintech: a payments and collections product with financing on top. Over half of revenue appears to come from financing, so it leans toward lending, but the payments software is substantive.

Outside mandate. Settlr is raising a INR 30 Cr Series A at INR 180 Cr post and seeking a lead, with four Series A funds in conversation, after a INR 9 Cr institutional seed. The model needs a payment aggregator to keep processing card-funded rent to landlords. In September 2025, under RBI's PA directions, that permission was effectively withdrawn for this flow: CRED, PhonePe and Paytm stopped because landlords were not KYC-onboarded merchants. criteria.rationale: For an earned-wage-access lender the defining risk is who holds credit and non-recovery risk, and under what licence. Nothing is said about non-recovery when a worker leaves before payroll, and the listed risks are regulation and payroll integration, not default. Per C004, leaning on an NBFC partner is a low R1, which takes this from ~1 to 0.5.
